reviewPurpose: Follow up five exact-locality GBIF zeroes with source-backed name variants and accessible fish-source alternatives; do not infer absence.

queryParameters.locality: one exact source-quoted string per request

queries.queryRole: published-study-name; documented alias of registry name Ticub Lake
LLDA report title/map label; system wording, not a separate alias
LLDA sampling-station label; a reach/station, not a river alias
official WQMA/system label; umbrella geography, not an alias for Dumacaa River alone
official report wording naming the component rivers separately; not an alias for Dumacaa alone
spelling variant in article body text; not adopted as an alias because the article title consistently uses Lagadlarin

gbifFollowUp.result: All six additional exact source-string queries returned zero rows. No coordinates, polygons, taxon filters, or other providers were queried in this follow-up.

waterbodyIdentityReviews.nameDecision: No well-supported alternate river name was adopted in this pass. A 2014 goby study uses Maragondon River directly; the phrase San Diego River found only in a third-party copy of an unverified watershed report and was not added as an alias.
Retain Tanay River as the waterbody name. Tanay River System is an official LLDA report label; Mouth of Tanay River is one named station/reach, not a whole-river alias.
Retain Dumacaa River. Iyam-Dumacaa River System/WQMA describes an umbrella watershed with two rivers, not a synonym or duplicate for Dumacaa River.
Retain Lagadlarin Mangrove Forest. Lagardlarin appears in body/table text in one study but not its title; treat it as a likely typographic/OCR variant, not a verified alias.
Add Tikub Lake as a source-supported alias of the existing Ticub Lake lead. The fish-survey article locates Tikub Lake in Tiaong, Quezon and names Barangays Ayusan I and San Pedro.

alternativeSourceReviews.bibliography: Bayot, F. A. A., Joya, K. N. A., & Jacinto, W. R. (2014). Phylogenetic analysis and barcoding of gobies in Maragondon River, Cavite, Philippines. International Journal of Current Science, 12, E50-E56.
alternativeSourceReviews.rightsReview: The publisher page declares CC BY 4.0. Reuse terms do not resolve the source's biological identification conflicts.

sourceFactsHeld.sampleContext: Three pre-collected goby phenotypes; the article cites an unpublished 2011 study and says voucher specimens were sent to the Philippine National Museum for verification, but does not report a verification outcome.
identityConflicts: A1 has a conflicting morphological identification in the article and the authors discuss inconsistent morphometrics.
B2 is assigned conflicting goby names across the article's morphology, BLAST and phylogenetic discussion.
The article itself calls the molecular identifications putative and recommends further sequence verification.

alternativeSourceReviews.accessReview: Complete seven-page publisher PDF and publisher landing-page license text reviewed online; no local PDF copy retained.
limits: The study is a historical goby lead, not a complete river inventory or current-presence survey.
No exact sampling reach or coordinates are adopted.
No species-level claim is admitted until identity conflicts are independently resolved.

alternativeSourceReviews.bibliography: Labatos, B. V. Jr., & Briones, N. D. (2014). Freshwater Fishes of Tikub Lake, Tiaong, Quezon, Philippines. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 5(1), 41-53. DOI: 10.7828/ajob.v5i1.480.

sourceFactsHeld.abstractReports: A historical survey of 221 individuals and nine species; the abstract names two most-abundant taxa.
sourceFactsHeld.waterbodyLocality: Tikub Lake, Tiaong, Quezon; Barangays Ayusan I and San Pedro.
sourceFactsHeld.fullArticle: ResearchGate identifies an author-uploaded public full text; the publisher landing page requires login or registration for its full text. Exact sampling calendar dates were not confirmed in this follow-up.

alternativeSourceReviews.reuseReview: No item-specific license was verified. The author-upload page warns that content may be subject to copyright. Do not transcribe the species table into a public dataset until the reuse basis is established.
limits: A 2014 survey is historical and is not a current or complete lake checklist.
The article's study results do not establish current abundance, native status today, catchability, legal access or safety.
The alias query Tikub Lake returned zero GBIF occurrence rows; that is not evidence of fish absence.

alternativeSourceReviews.title: Water Quality Assessment Report - Tanay River
alternativeSourceReviews.sourceFactsHeld: The official LLDA report maps five water-quality stations, including the river mouth at Barangay Wawa, Plaza Aldea, a Manila East Road bridge, a headwater, and Daranak Falls.

alternativeSourceReviews.title: Geospatial Biodiversity Assessment of Lagadlarin Mangrove Forest in Lobo, Batangas, Philippines, for Sustainable Ecotourism
alternativeSourceReviews.sourceFactsHeld: The 2024 article surveys mangrove and mangrove-associate flora, not fish. Its title uses Lagadlarin; one body-text extraction uses Lagardlarin.
The alternate journal-volume PDF contains the same conference abstract on printed page 40, without the complete fish table or exact sampling dates.
A third-party user-catch page reports two catches but does not provide a source-reviewed fish inventory or auditable specimen/observation evidence.

nonClaims: No zero-result GBIF query establishes fish absence.
No species names from these held research leads were added to a public projection.
A water-quality station or watershed/system label is not a fish occurrence or a substitute river boundary.
No alias is adopted from the unverified San Diego River third-party-copy wording or the likely Lagadlarin/Lagardlarin typo.
No municipal-water boundary, present-day abundance, fishing permission, safety, diet or bait claim is added.
